params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# WHAT THIS AGENT ASKS ITS OWN MODEL FOR, declared beside the agent and not in a
# collector one composite away.
#
# WHY IT LIVES HERE. Whoever is REACHED declares themselves -- the rule GH #552
# wrote for tool schemas and GH #606 read one word wider for the sections of the
# `sidecar` block. The splitter that cuts the block knows no section, and the
# collector that composes the contract merges the `sidecar[]` offers of everyone
# who answers its menu question. So a section costs an OFFER: no line in the
# splitter, no line in the collector, and no lane in this composite's own
# contract.
#
# THIS CELL DECLARES NO TOOL, on purpose. The tools of a `talky` are the
# parent's -- `./collector`'s `params.tools` names them and the hives that
# answer them declare them -- and a name typed here would be a name nothing in
# this composite answers. `SCHEMAS` is empty and stays empty; what this cell has
# to say is the other half of the same question.
SCHEMAS = []

# THE THREE SECTIONS OF THE ADVISE MODE.
#
# A duplex voice call turns this agent from the speaker into the ADVISER: the
# voice model is the one talking to the caller, on its own timeline, and what
# this agent produces is what that model should say, know and obey -- never a
# reply of its own. The block is where that advice travels, one key per kind,
# because the three are consumed differently: `fact` is paraphrased aloud,
# `context` is never spoken by itself, and `correction` outlives the turn it
# arrived on.
#
# OPTIONAL, ALL THREE, and the emptiness outside a duplex call is stated in the
# words of the offers rather than switched by a second mechanism. A section is
# offered once, at composition time, and the same block contract stands in the
# brain for every turn the agent takes; a section marked required would be a
# section the model is told to write on turns where it means nothing, which is
# the failure the collector's own preamble was rewritten to avoid (GH #606).
# `in advise mode only` is therefore part of every instruction: the mode is on
# the turn (`system.instructions.mode`), the sections are in the contract, and
# the model reads both.
FACT = ("in advise mode only: what the caller should HEAR next, as one or two"
        " plain sentences the voice model will paraphrase. Facts only; no"
        " greetings, no questions the model can ask itself.")

CONTEXT = ("in advise mode only: what the voice model should KNOW silently --"
           " memory recall, profile, application state. Never spoken on its"
           " own.")

# SPARINGLY, and the reason is that nothing takes it back: a correction changes
# how the voice model behaves for the rest of the call, and there is no event on
# the model's timeline that would expire one.
CORRECTION = ("in advise mode only: a rule that changes the model's behaviour"
              " for the REST of the call (a guardrail, a redirect). Sparingly:"
              " it never expires.")

# Each section is ONE plain sentence or two, so each schema is a string and the
# collector renders the example out of its description (`skeleton_of`). An
# object here would ask a model mid-call to get a shape right on top of getting
# the advice right.
def _section(name, instruction, shape):
    return {"section": name, "required": False,
            "schema": {"type": "string", "description": shape},
            "instruction": instruction}


SIDECAR = [
    _section("fact", FACT, "one or two sentences the model paraphrases aloud"),
    _section("context", CONTEXT, "what the model should know and not say"),
    _section("correction", CORRECTION, "a rule for the rest of the call"),
]

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc["body"]
asked = body.get("tools")

# A NAME IS NAMED BACK, never dropped. This cell serves no tool, so every name
# it is handed is one it has nothing under, and a caller learns that from the
# answer rather than from a silence. `*` asks for everything this cell declares,
# which is nothing, and is not an unknown name.
#
# There is no `tools_missing` here, and that is the difference to a hive of
# tools: the offer is not a response to a name. The answer travels on this lane
# whatever arrived on it -- a menu answer being fanned in carries no `tools`
# slot at all -- because a section is what this agent asks for, not what it was
# asked about.
names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)] if isinstance(asked, list) else []
seen, unknown = set(), []
for n in names:
    if n == "*" or n in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(n)
    unknown.append(n)

header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": 0,
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": header, "schemas": SCHEMAS, "unknown": unknown,
    "sidecar": SIDECAR, "messages": []}))

description.purpose: What this agent asks its OWN model for, handed to the collector inside the same composite: the three sections of the `sidecar` block that carry ADVICE to a voice model -- `fact`, `context` and `correction`. Whoever is reached declares themselves (GH #552), read one word wider for the block a splitter cuts (GH #606): the sections live beside the agent that consumes them rather than as a literal in a collector one composite away, and they cost no line in the splitter, none in the collector and no lane in this composite's contract. It declares NO tool: the tools of a `talky` are the parent's, named in `./collector`'s `params.tools` and declared by whoever answers them.
description.use_when: Reached on this composite's own `in_menu` fan, beside `./collector`, and answered back into that collector as a second menu answerer. Never addressed by name, never part of a tool round: it answers no `tool_call` and carries no `tool_name`. The edge that carries its answer stamps `context.tool_answerer`, or the merge that keeps every answerer's submenu in one row per answerer would let this cell and a tools hive overwrite each other's half on every tick (GH #529).
description.not_in_scope: No tool schema, ever -- see purpose. No judgement about WHEN the three sections apply: that is one sentence in each instruction (`in advise mode only`) and one slot on the turn (`system.instructions.mode`), and a cell that decided it would be deciding it once, at composition time, for every turn the agent takes. And no FENCE: the offer says what belongs under each key and never how many blocks an answer carries or what they open with -- that frame belongs to the collector that composes every section into one contract (GH #606).
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: always empty -- this cell declares no tool. unknown[]: every name it was handed, verbatim and deduplicated, because it serves none of them; `*` asks for everything it declares, which is nothing, and is not an unknown name. hop.error_code `tool_unknown` when that list is non-empty. sidecar[]: the three sections, `{section, required, schema, instruction}`, all three optional. It travels on EVERY answer of this cell, including one that was handed no `tools` slot at all: a section is not a response to a name. The asking collector merges the offers of all its answerers into one block contract.
description.consumes_meaning: body.tools: the names the asking collector declares it uses, if the fan happens to carry them. Optional in every sense -- the answer is the same without it, because what this cell has to say is what it ASKS FOR and not what it was asked about.
examples: {"tools":[]} -> no schemas, no unknown, sidecar[] with the three sections
{"tools":["*"]} -> the same: `*` asks for everything this cell declares, which is nothing
{"tools":["web_search"]} -> unknown ["web_search"], hop.error_code `tool_unknown` -- a tools hive answers that one
a menu answer fanned in, carrying no `tools` slot -> the same three offers, and no error
